children: The lender will issue rated, listed and unsecured subordinated debentures through private placement to strengthen its capital base
Equitas Small Finance Bank’s board has approved raising up to Rs 500 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) on a private placement basis.

The board approved the issue of up to 50,000 rated, listed, unsecured, subordinated, transferable and redeemable NCDs, with a face value of Rs 1 lakh each. The securities will be issued in a single series and will qualify as Lower Tier II capital under the Basel II capital adequacy framework.

The fundraise is part of the bank’s broader capital-raising plan. In June, Equitas Small Finance Bank had approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 1,750 crore, including Rs 1,250 crore through a qualified institutional placement and up to Rs 500 crore through debt securities.

The latest issue will add to the bank’s capital base and provide funds for its corporate requirements. Equitas has previously used NCD issuances to augment its Tier-II capital and meet general corporate purposes.
The bank had issued Rs 500 crore of NCDs in July 2025 at a coupon rate of 9.6 per cent, with the securities scheduled to mature in July 2030.
The latest issue remains subject to the applicable regulatory and other requirements.
Equitas Small Finance Bank has been pursuing a larger capital-raising programme as it works to strengthen its balance sheet and support future business growth.

The board’s June approval provided for both equity and debt fundraising, with the enabling resolutions subsequently placed before shareholders at the bank’s annual general meeting on 9 September 2026.
The latest Rs 500-crore NCD issue will therefore form the debt component of the bank’s broader capital-raising plan.
